docs.title: GlobalProtect VPN drops every few minutes on Windows 11 24H2
docs.body:
ORBIT IT KNOWLEDGE BASE | CONFIDENTIAL - INTERNAL USE ONLY
Document owner: IT Service Desk | Last reviewed: 2026-08-14 | Revision 7
----
Symptom: after the Windows 11 24H2 feature update, GlobalProtect 6.2.0 and 6.2.1 disconnect every 8-12 minutes, mostly on Wi-Fi. The tunnel re-establishes automatically but active Teams calls and RDP sessions drop.
Cause: a known incompatibility between the 24H2 network stack and the GlobalProtect 6.2.x split-tunnel driver when the adapter renegotiates its DHCP lease.
Fix: upgrade GlobalProtect to 6.2.4 or later from Company Portal (category Network). Reboot after the upgrade. If 6.2.4 is not yet visible in Company Portal, IT can push it to the device from Intune within 15 minutes.
Workaround until upgraded: in GlobalProtect settings set Connect Method to 'On-demand' and reconnect manually after lease renewal.
----

docs.title: Wi-Fi adapter power saving causes VPN disconnects
docs.body:
ORBIT IT KNOWLEDGE BASE | CONFIDENTIAL - INTERNAL USE ONLY
Document owner: IT Service Desk | Last reviewed: 2026-08-14 | Revision 7
----
Symptom: VPN disconnects when the laptop is idle for a few minutes on battery, on any network.
Cause: Windows lets the Wi-Fi adapter power down to save energy; the VPN tunnel times out.
Fix: Device Manager > Network adapters > (Wi-Fi adapter) > Power Management > untick 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power'. On ThinkPads also set Lenovo Vantage > Power > Intelligent Cooling to 'Balanced'.
Note: this does not explain disconnects while the laptop is actively in use or plugged in.
----

docs.title: VPN instability on hotel and captive-portal networks (MTU)
docs.body:
ORBIT IT KNOWLEDGE BASE | CONFIDENTIAL - INTERNAL USE ONLY
Document owner: IT Service Desk | Last reviewed: 2026-08-14 | Revision 7
----
Symptom: VPN connects but pages stall or the tunnel drops on hotel, airport or conference Wi-Fi with a captive portal. Home networks work fine.
Cause: these networks often use a smaller MTU; large VPN packets are fragmented or dropped.
Fix: GlobalProtect 6.2.4+ negotiates MTU automatically. On older clients, IT can apply the 'VPN-MTU-1300' Intune profile. Always complete the captive portal login in a browser before connecting the VPN.
How to tell: if drops happen on home Wi-Fi too, MTU is unlikely to be the main cause.
----

docs.title: Set up a network printer
docs.body:

Document owner: IT Service Desk | Last reviewed: 2026-08-14 | Revision 7
----

docs.title: Outlook calendar not syncing
docs.body:
ORBIT IT KNOWLEDGE BASE | CONFIDENTIAL - INTERNAL USE ONLY
Document owner: IT Service Desk | Last reviewed: 2026-08-14 | Revision 7
----
If meetings are missing from Outlook, switch off 'New Outlook' and back on, then run File > Account Settings > Repair. Shared calendars can take up to 2 hours to appear after permissions change. Mobile calendar issues are usually fixed by removing and re-adding the account in the Outlook app.

docs.title: Laptop refresh programme
docs.body:
ORBIT IT KNOWLEDGE BASE | CONFIDENTIAL - INTERNAL USE ONLY
Document owner: IT Service Desk | Last reviewed: 2026-08-14 | Revision 7
----

docs.title: Travel checklist for international trips
docs.body:
ORBIT IT KNOWLEDGE BASE | CONFIDENTIAL - INTERNAL USE ONLY
Document owner: IT Service Desk | Last reviewed: 2026-08-14 | Revision 7
----
Before travelling: install pending updates, confirm VPN works from a non-office network, register your trip in the travel portal (required for Singapore, Japan and the US), and pack a USB-C charger. Some countries restrict VPN use; check the travel portal country page.
